newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Ahmanson prefers friendly deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ahmanson prefers friendly deal.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co President and Chief Operating Officer Bruce Willison Tuesday said Ahmanson would prefer a friendly merger with Great Western Financial Corp but the thrift is prepared for a hostile takeover should its offer be rejected.
"We're emphasising our desire to have a negotiated transaction, but we're taking the usual legal steps to ensure our position," Willison said in a telephone interview.
Earlier, the Los Angeles based thrift offered to acquire rival Great Western in a $6 billion stock deal.

Great Western has said it is reviewing the offer, under which Ahmanson would swap 1.05 of its shares for each Great Western share. The bid values Great Western at $42.53 a share, representing a 24.2 percent premium over Great Western's closing stock price last Friday.
Willison said there had been "conceptual discussions" between the two thrifts about a year ago, but the talks failed to produce a deal.
He said Ahmanson's offer was a way to get those talks going again.
"Sometimes you need to put a firm offer on the table to get discussions kick-started," Willison said.
"It was our sense that the overall strategic and financial rationales for this deal were so compelling that it encouraged us to move forward."

To strengthen its case, Ahmanson filed a lawsuit in Delaware Tuesday seeking to block Great Western's poison pill. The thrift also hired proxy solicitation firm MacKenzie Partners Inc and proposed to nominate three individuals to Great Western's board of directors.
"We believe that three individuals we've nominated can certainly make their voices known with regard to the worthiness of our transaction," Willison said.

When asked if Ahmanson would raise its bid in the event of a rival bidder coming in with a sweeter offer, Willison said: "We feel very good about the prmeium being offered and feel it represents a great value to shareholders."
Willison said Ahmanson was meeting with shareholders Tuesday to explain the proposed transaction.
"We're aware we have a large overlap of shareholders with Great Western," he said.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission Tuesday, Ahmanson said it hired Credit Suisse First Boston and Montgomery Securities as advisors. The thrift also said it purchased 100 shares of Great Western stock last Thursday for $32.50.
The company said it also had informal discussions on "a number of occasions" during the last several years regarding a merger.
On Monday, Ahmanson Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Rinehart contacted Great Western's President and Chief Executive Officer John Maher about a possible tax-free merger.
A spokesman said that 38 of Ahmanson's 50 largest shareholders are also shareholders in Great Western.
Great Western's shareholder meeting is set for late April, but Willison said he believed a speedy transaction was in the best interests of the institutions, consumers and shareholders.
